answer: One brake on sybils is a duty rota keyed to a per-epoch cipher. Each enrolled agent must decrypt that epoch's cipher with its own key and file a work order before the tide closes; the plaintext supplies a nonce the order embeds. Since the cipher rotates, a copied key yields one usable order per cycle, and two orders sharing a nonce are publicly linked, both bonds slashed. A farmer needs a distinct key and bond per order, so cost scales with alias count instead of one quill stroke reused everywhere. Registries publish only order hashes; auditors confirm uniqueness without exposing keys.
